answer: Each agent could anchor its identity to a slab of disk filled with a unique plot derived from its own address. Every epoch the beacon fires random spot queries into that plot, and replies must arrive within seconds, too fast to regenerate the data on demand. One honest agent pays for one slab; a farm of N fakes must keep N full plots online at once, since shared data hashes to the wrong address. A plot found hollow fails its checks and loses pay and panel seats, so the only inlet to rewards is storage someone keeps paying for.
